title: Parent Plan — Seven-Week Grade 3 Science Bridge

baseline.preservation: The completed Science Baseline remains a separate, locked assessment under its existing storage key. Course work must never replace, rescore, or reopen it.
strengths: Substantial sampled prior-grade Life Science strength
Substantial sampled prior-grade Earth Science strength
Grade 3 readiness shown with magnetic forces acting without contact
Grade 3 readiness shown by comparing weather records
Grade 3 readiness shown by using fossils as evidence about past life
Grade 3 readiness shown by selecting an engineering solution to reduce flood damage
reinforceThroughUse: Direct observation versus inference, judgment, prediction, or opinion
Flexible versus rigid and other observable material properties
Identifying evidence that actually supports a claim
Separating measured or observed data from expectations or opinions
Comparing engineering solutions from test results
Understanding the purpose and limits of models and plans
newGrade3Instruction: Inherited traits versus learned or acquired characteristics
Environmental effects on growth and survival
Deeper investigation of magnetic forces acting without contact
baseline.interpretation: This is an instructional bridge. Do not assign broad remediation in areas where Rory already demonstrated strength. Ask what he observed or measured before accepting an explanation. When results differ from a prediction, praise accurate reporting and help him revise the claim.

reviewStatuses: Review together in a fresh task

weeks.title: Thinking Like a Scientist
weeks.parentRole: Release equal papers from the same height and protect fair-test conditions. Ask, ‘What did you actually see or count?’
lookFor: Observation language describes visible or measured events
Evidence comes from the four recorded trials
The claim changes if the results differ from the prediction
exitIntent: Direct observation is ‘The leaf is green.’
Relevant evidence is the recorded trial count
A prediction comes before the test and is not measured test data

weeks.title: Materials and Changes
weeks.parentRole: Prepare equal-size samples and equal water amounts. Handle refreezing and spills.
lookFor: Flexible and rigid are based on bending observations
Material choice cites water-test results
Melting/refreezing is reversible; torn paper cannot return to one unbroken sheet through the tested actions
exitIntent: Flexible means bends easily
The result with zero drops passing through best resists water
The refrozen water observation supports reversibility

weeks.title: Forces and Motion
weeks.parentRole: Partner in opposite pulls and supervise magnets and small parts. Keep car release position constant.
lookFor: Pulling a wagon handle is identified as a pull
No motion change with equal opposite pulls supports balanced forces
The paper-layer gap is cited as evidence for no-contact magnetic force
exitIntent: Wagon handle toward the person is a pull
Equal opposite forces with no change in motion are balanced
Movement across a visible gap is the relevant magnetic evidence

weeks.title: Life Cycles
weeks.parentRole: Help prepare seeds and the rotating model. Let Rory place stages and explain arrows.
lookFor: Butterfly order is egg, caterpillar, pupa, adult
Models are circular and include offspring or new seeds
Rory explains both a shared pattern and a difference
exitIntent: Egg → caterpillar → pupa → adult
Arrows show sequence and continuation
Organisms begin life, grow, reproduce, and eventually die while offspring continue the cycle

weeks.title: Traits
weeks.parentRole: Set safe watering amounts and help keep other conditions steady. Record scribing or guidance honestly.
lookFor: Natural fur color is likely inherited
A trained trick is learned
The growth claim stays cautious and cites measurements even when results are unclear
exitIntent: Natural fur color is inherited
A trained trick is learned
The answer must use Rory’s actual measurements rather than an expected result

weeks.title: Earth Science Through Evidence
weeks.parentRole: Join outdoor observations and help Rory distinguish a short weather record from long-term climate data.
lookFor: A weather claim cites supplied values
A prediction is labeled separately
Fossil conclusions include both a supported idea and an evidence limit
exitIntent: Conditions today are weather
A fossil leaf supports that a plant lived long ago
Relevant evidence names exact seasonal values

weeks.title: Engineering Design
weeks.parentRole: Control equal water pours, supervise cutting and spills, and require the same test conditions for both designs.
lookFor: Criteria and constraints are named before building
A plan is treated as an idea, not proof
Design B responds to a recorded failure point
The final choice cites at least two test results
exitIntent: A plan must be tested
Criteria describe success and constraints describe limits
The stronger solution is selected from test data rather than appearance or preference
